texts.preamble: Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Kabc020348222022 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City Scch-17 Present: Sri. Kanchi Mayanna Goutam B.A.L, Ll.M., Member, Mact Xix Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated this the 3rd day of October- 2024 Mvc No.6506/2024 Petitioner/S: Sri Rangaiah, C/o Sri Magadi Rangaiah, Aged about 50 years, Working as Labourer/Lorry Loader, R/at No.165, Kote Street, Nelamangala Taluk, Thyamagondlu, Bengaluru Rural- 562 132, Karnataka. (By Sri. Narasimharaju, Adv.,) V/s. Respondents: 1.The General Manager, K.S.R.T.C., Shanthi Nagar, Bengaluru - 560 027. (By Sri. Mahadevaiah,Adv.,) 2. Sri Jagadeesh Nayak, Scch-17 2 Mvc No.6506/2022 Aged Major, R/at Machihalli, Thanda, Telgi Hobli, Harappanahalli Taluk, Davanagere District-583131 (Exparte) Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02.07.2022. 2. The petition averments in brief are as under: On 02.07.2022 at about 9.45 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Tumakuru Traffic Police station at Ashoka Road, Health Canteen Cross, the petitioner was proceeding to KSRTC bus stand to board the bus in order to go to his village, at that time the driver KSRTC bus bearing Reg. NO.KA-06-F-1173 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and the left side back wheel of the bus ran over on both the legs of the claimant and thereby he sustained grievous crush injuries to both legs and all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to General Hospital, Tumakuru and later he was shifted to Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, B.H. Road, Tumakuru wherein he was admitted as inpatient and the left leg of the petitioner was amputed. He has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc., Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as a Loader of vegetable to Lorry under package system and was earning Rs.1,500/- per day and in week days he used to earn Rs.2,000/- to Rs.3,000/- per day. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability. The respondent No.1 is the owner and internal insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. NO.KA-06-F-1173 and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending bus, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notices respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel, but the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the tribunal, hence, placed exparte. The 1st respondent has appeared and filed written statement by denying that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. NO.KA-06-F-1173. Further contended that the bus was proceeding from Tumkur Depot No.2 towards bus stand, Tumkur and it was driven by its driver in a slow and cautious manner and while took turn towards bus station, Tumkur, petitioner/pedestrian consumed alcohol without following traffic rules and regulations came in zig-zag motion, lost control over himself while crossing the road and fell down on the road, his leg touched to left side back wheel of the said bus, suffered injuries. Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it. Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/ 2 5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 22. Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P23 to 27. First respondent examined the driver of the offending KSRTC bus/2nd respondent as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 to 5. 6.

By relying on the about quoted judgment the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 argued that the contents of charge sheet cannot be relied by the tribunal and the evidence lead by the parties has Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/ 4 to be considered independently. No doubt that the contents of charge sheet cannot be considered as a conclusive evidence and proof while deciding the fact of negligence. The respondents contended that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol and he himself by his negligence came under the left side portion of the bus. 13. Another defence is taken by the respondent No.1 that as the petitioner was crossing the road it is expected that even he was the negligent and the contributory negligence has to be considered. In this regard the respondent relied on the judgment reported in ILR 1988 KAR 1934 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between Sri Narasimhaiah V/s The General Manager & another wherein it is held as follows: 7. The appellant in this case was a pedestrian who virtually walked into the path of the vehicle and got injured. There is a wrong notion which prevails that pedestrains have the birth-right to wander around the stroll on the roads according to their whims and fancies and that even if they make every effort to get run over, that the vehicle drivers are supposed to still try and save them. It has been pointed out in this judgment that the rules of the road require pedestrians to avoid strolling on to the road and that the roads can be crossed only at designated places. A breach of these rules immediately holds the pedestrain liable for negligence and if it is demonstrated that the injury of death occurred due to the negligence of the pedestrain, the driver of the vehicle, the owner and the insurer would then be entitled to disclaim their liability. In this regard, I rely on the reportable decision, in Civil Appeal No.2476/2019 in the case of M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., decided on 05.03.2019, the Hon'ble supreme court has held as follows, "We may now summarize the principles discussed above: Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/ 7 In Kajal Vs. Jaidish Chand reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 127, it is held that it would be appropriate to adopt the system of multiplier to award the compensation under the head 'Attendant Charges' as the claimant would require the care of an attendant for the rest of his life. g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life: The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived his of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
